text: can I attach the nook drive on this machine and on my desktop at the same time, so both can write to it?

arg: nook list 2>&1; echo '---'; nook disk 2>&1 | head -20

text:
No — and `nook attach` will refuse to let you.

The network drive is a raw block device. Whichever machine attaches it puts an ext4 filesystem on top and assumes it owns the disk exclusively — it caches metadata and never learns about writes coming from anywhere else. Two machines attached read-write corrupts the image, and the damage shows up long after the mistake. `nook attach` asks the Pi who holds the drive first and stops if the answer isn't "nobody".

Right now nothing holds it:

```
disk    not attached (nbd)
export  nook @ 100.x.y.z:10809
attached none
```

So you can attach here, but then you'd need `nook eject` before the desktop can take it.

**What you actually want is the shared folder.** `/mnt/nook/files` over SFTP is safe for many machines at once — that's the whole reason there are two lanes:

```bash
nook mount        # ~/nook/nook, on both machines
```

Both can read and write concurrently, and containers on the Pi see the same files. Use the network drive only when you specifically want USB-stick behaviour on one machine at a time.
